front: Section A — marks and assessment objective
back: 10 marks, AO1: identify, analyse and research.

front: Where does Section A evidence go?
back: In your informal sketchbook — it is exploratory, so it can be rough as long as it is clear.

front: How many WJEC contexts should you analyse?
back: All three, before choosing one. Then find at least three possible directions within your chosen context.
Data you collect yourself, directly from users or the real world — surveys, interviews, observations and measurements.
Data already collected by others that you find and use — e.g. existing product analysis, designers, standards, materials.
Discovery, not confirmation — researching the context and your users to work out what to design. Never ask 'would you buy my product?'
Aim for 5–10, mixing mostly closed questions (easy to graph) with one or two open questions.
Screening (who is the user?), Behaviour (what do they do now?), Frustrations (where is the opportunity?), Priorities (what matters to them?).
A question that pushes a particular answer, e.g. 'Don't you agree storage is a problem?' It biases results.
Aesthetics, Cost, Customer, Environment, Size, Safety, Function, Materials — a framework for analysing existing products.

front: How many existing products to analyse?
back: Four, using ACCESS FM, each with annotated images and a 'What this tells me' sentence.
Draws together survey findings and product analyses: user needs, what existing products do well and poorly, and materials, sizes or features to consider.
Key user needs and wants, at least three design problems or opportunities, and 2–3 possible design briefs with advantages and disadvantages.
Band 4 asks for a broad range of opportunities that inform possible briefs; showing several then choosing one is the clearest evidence.
Thorough research linked to context and professionals, detailed analysis of user needs, and a broad range of problems and opportunities.
50% of the GCSE, 100 marks, about 35 hours, from one of three WJEC contexts. Teacher-marked and moderated; the final prototype is made under supervision in school.
Keep going round design → model → test → reflect, improving each time — WJEC calls it the interaction of mind and hand.
